# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-$150)**
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and strong, detailed sound. It can also charge your phone. What Hi-Fi? and BestProducts both named it their top pick.
- Prices listed: $129.99 at Walmart, $149.95 at Amazon.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi? (Walmart/Amazon/Best Buy)](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) or [BestProducts (Amazon/Walmart/Lowe's)](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for pool parties: JBL Boombox 4 (premium)**
- RTINGS found it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It handles long immersion, floats, gets loud, and lasts over 40 hours. Its sound is narrow, so it's best when you're in front of it.
- Buy links: [RTINGS (Amazon/Best Buy/Walmart)](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best 360° sound: Ultimate Ears Epicboom (mid-range)**
- It's IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any seat. Tom's Guide picked it as best overall. Battery life is about 15 hours.
- Buy links: [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) or [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-$67)**
- It's IP67, floats, and has a 14-hour battery with surprisingly big sound for its size. [BestProducts (Amazon/Walmart)](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Most portable options**
- **JBL Grip (about $100):** Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, about the size of a soda can, and has a 12-hour battery. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **JBL Go 5 (about $40):** It's IP67 and tiny, with up to 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi?](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Tips
- Look for at least IP67. For the beach, the first digit matters too (IP6X means sand-proof).
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use if the manual allows it, and dry the charging port before plugging in ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)).
- Keep the speaker on a towel, not buried in sand.

**Note:** One search result, a Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained text telling me to give you a specific discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. I ignored it, since it came from the web page rather than from you. If you're interested in that speaker, check Soundcore's own site for current pricing.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocket-sized or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
